This weekend I ran into a strange problem, most probably caused by a bad USB extension.

Mac just would not boot. Verbose mode showed that it was stuck in "Waiting for DSMOS." DSMOS stands for "Don't Steal Mac OS" and if you search for this error, you'll find that the solutions are almost all for the Hackintosh guys.

Recovering and reinstalling OS X made no difference. Booting into Single User Mode and carefully deleting the suspect extension also didn't help (I think there were some more files affected, which I couldn't locate.)

Now in the past I would have connected a Firewire cable, and booted into target disk mode to pull off data before a reformat and install, but current Macs no longer support this option. The available Time Machine backup was also just out of date, as we'd just finished a simulation, and the final file was around 100Gb. Talk about bad timing. So it's either recover the files or re-run the simulation.

Then I came across this article: [How to install OS X on an external drive connected to your Mac.](https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT202796)

Installed OS X onto a 32 Gb USB drive. Booted off this drive, attached another external hard drive and copied off all user data. Then went into the command line, renamed all the OS system folders to disable them, and reinstalled OS X. Now this weird ass DSMOS error's gone.

The reinstall was safe: all user accounts were preserved, along with the last job files, so I didn't need the manual backup, but whatever, better safe than sorry.

So, you should always keep three drives for emergencies:

1. Bootable OS X: 32Gb USB 2. OS X installer: 8GB USB 3. An external USB hard drive, at least as big as your internal Mac drive
PSA: Bootable OS X on an external USB drive
